learned_patterns.pattern: A full 15-day outage (2026-06-30 -> 07-15) with no CLU session and no Signal Engine run. The §2.5 staleness guard did its job — this session refused new entries on 15-day-old signals — but the entire automation stack was dark, and an agentic INTC sell still executed on 07-07 with no session logging it. Lesson: the guard prevents BAD trades but not silent drift; broker reconciliation is the only reliable state source across a gap, and Signal Engine uptime is the true prerequisite for the strategy to function at all.

Second confirmed instance of an untracked agentic fill surfacing only via reconciliation — first JEPQ (buy, 06-30), now INTC (sell, 07-07). Untracked agentic orders both open and CLOSE positions between sessions. Always reconcile positions AND recent orders every session and resolve conflicts to the broker (§5.1), never to prose memory.

INTC exited at -14.98% (entry $128.21 -> $109.01). Its ATR-based stop was ~12.6% ($112.06); the agentic market sell landed a bit below it, roughly consistent with a stop-driven exit on a high-vol name (ATR 7.6% at entry). High-ATR single names generate wide stops and large realized losses when they roll over — reinforces keeping LAB small and tech-weighted vs concentrated single-name risk.

On the last live matrix (06-30) composites read NEUTRAL/BEARISH while price ripped; 15 days later NVDA is +5.6% and ARKK +3.4% from entry despite BEARISH/NEUTRAL stale composites, while SOXX (NEUTRAL) fell -6.2%. Confirms the composite lags fast moves in both directions and should never be read as a forward call in isolation — the §4.1 5-gate check (with Trend + MACD) is the authorization, not the composite.
